sources.entry: KubeMonitor - KubeMonitor is a macOS app that displays information about your active Kubernetes cluster in your menu bar.

summary.one_liner: KubeMonitor is a macOS menu bar app that shows the state of your active Kubernetes cluster by polling kubectl for pods and nodes.
summary.what_it_does: KubeMonitor runs in the macOS menu bar and periodically calls the kubectl command to gather information about running pods and nodes. It lists pods, which can be grouped by a label and color-coded by current state. Resource information from pods and nodes is compiled into pie charts showing cluster health, with tooltips for individual pods or groups. Users can open a terminal that SSHes into the node a pod runs on, or launch a kubectl exec session into a container. Active pods can be deleted from the GUI, and the cluster name is shown at the top of the window.
use_cases: monitor Kubernetes pods from the macOS menu bar
check cluster node and pod resource usage
group and color-code pods by label or state
open a shell into a pod's container
SSH into the node a pod is running on
kill a pod without using the command line
how_to_run: Install kubectl (default lookup path is ~/Documents/google-cloud-sdk/bin/, changeable in settings)
Run `pod install` in the project directory to fetch CocoaPods dependencies
Open the generated KubeMonitor.xcworkspace file and build it in Xcode
notable: Groups pods by a user-chosen label and color-codes them by state
Pie charts summarize cluster health from pod and node resource data
One-click SSH into the node hosting a pod, using Google Cloud SSH keys by default
Opens kubectl exec sessions directly into containers
caveats: macOS only; requires kubectl and an Xcode build with CocoaPods
SSH to nodes needs key-based authentication; default keys assume Google Cloud (~/.ssh/google_compute_engine)
README states it is not an official Google product; no maintenance status is given
keywords: see what my cluster is doing
kill a pod from a gui
